Cc: procure@procureco.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: MAP weekly: initial latency/throughput snapshot

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We ran the guardrail workloads overnight and attached the raw latency/throughput snapshot (acme_latency_report_q4.csv). High-level notes:

- P95 latency (Prod load): 420ms on the 2xA5000 setup
- Sustained throughput: 310 rps before tail latency climbs
- KV cache hit rate: ~62% on the sample set

We want to align the MAP and close timeline with these performance realities. Two asks for this week's checkpoint:

1) Can Redwood supply a suggested tuning plan (batching / quantization / cache) with owners and risk levels?
2) Confirm whether Dedicated tier would hit our 99th percentile SLA at 400ms under our expected traffic profile.

I attached the run CSV and a short appendix of representative requests. Happy to jump on a 30m sync if useful.

Thanks,
Sara Nguyen
Sr. Engineering Manager, Platform
Acme Health

Attachment: acme_latency_report_q4.csv (CSV, 230KB)
From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP weekly: initial latency/throughput snapshot

Sara — thanks for the data and the clear asks. Short reply with a proposal and owners; I'll follow up with a more detailed MAP v2 (attached).

Summary proposal (owners & timeline):

- Quick tuning pass (48–72h) — owner: Monica Patel
  - Try conservative batching increase (batch_size +20%), enable prefix KV warmup for top 5 routes
  - Test window with synthetic load matching your 70/30 tail traffic
  - Risk: low (non-disruptive, reversible)

- Quantization validation (3–5 days) — owner: Vivek Kulkarni
  - Run int8 calibration on canary model; validate quality on the eval set from MAP appendix
  - Risk: medium (requires model variant + fallback path)

- Dedicated footprint check (ops + capacity) — owner: Laura Bennett
  - Validate whether Dedicated with 4xA5000 meets 99p @ 400ms for your traffic mix; include autoscale policy recommended margins
  - Risk: scheduling/cost trade-off, propose cost estimate by EOW

Immediate next steps:
- Monica to run the quick tuning pass and report P95/P99 deltas (ETA: 2026-12-03)
- Vivek to start quantization experiments in isolated env and share preliminary eval metrics (ETA: 2026-12-06)
- Laura to produce Dedicated sizing + cost delta (ETA: 2026-12-07)

I attached MAP-v2.pdf with the checklist and a proposed mutual action timeline toward close. If that looks good, can we lock a 30-minute checkpoint on Thursday at 9:30am PT?

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Lead Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: MAP-v2.pdf (PDF, 420KB)
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP weekly: initial latency/throughput snapshot

Quick update after the overnight synthetic window I ran against the CSV profile:

What I tried
- Increased batch target by 20% (server-side request grouping); warmup period 10m before load
- Enabled aggressive prefix KV population for the top-10 prefixes from your sample

Results (preliminary)
- P95 reduced from 420ms -> 360ms (20% improvement)
- Sustained throughput increased to ~380 rps before tail degradation
- KV hit rate jumped from 62% -> 81%

Action items (what I need)
- Sara: confirm the top-10 prefixes we should keep sticky for production vs. testing (small list of 10 example patterns)
- Vivek: can you run int8 validation on the same seed/requests I used and report on top-1 token divergence? If <= 0.5% we can promote to canary.
- Aditya/Laura: if we promote batching + KV tweaks to Dedicated, we need a safety rollback plan; I recommend a gradual canary rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) over 24h windows.

I'll push my run logs to the Drive folder and tag the runID.

- Monica
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
